# Resume Booster

> A live job board with zero ghost jobs: 700,000+ openings from 30,000+ company job boards, every posting pulled straight from the company's own hiring system (Workday, SmartRecruiters, Breezy, Oracle, Teamtailor, Personio, Pinpoint, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, BambooHR, Workable, Rippling, Recruitee, iCIMS, Paylocity, UKG Pro Recruiting, ADP Workforce Now, JazzHR, USAJOBS) — never an aggregator or a scrape. No dated posting older than 30 days (where a company publishes no date we keep the posting and show no age rather than invent one), the largest boards re-checked most often and the rotation running continuously (how far behind it is right now is a measurement rather than a promise: the live median and 95th-percentile re-check ages are published on the Ghost Job Index), every posting re-checked live at the moment of Apply, and the board audits its own accuracy daily and publishes the number ([/ghost-job-index](/ghost-job-index)). Free deterministic resume-fit scoring against any posting at [/jobs](/jobs). An AI apply agent reads your CV, ranks every live opening against it, writes a tailored application per role, answers the employer's own screening questions, and submits end-to-end on the hiring systems that permit it.

The companion tool is a free diagnostic resume scanner with verified output: an ATS score with a full point-by-point audit trail, every quoted line checked against the actual resume, per-vendor parsing checks (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, iCIMS), and keyword expectations sourced from the U.S. Department of Labor's O*NET database. 58 industries, 10 languages. Results are measured and reproducible (same document → same report ID), every resume quote is verified before display, and keyword expectations carry provenance. Free scan requires no signup and resumes are never stored.

Paid tools are one-time purchases: resume rewrites, cover letters, interview coaching, Freelance Boost (turns freelance/gig projects into recruiter-grade experience sections for career changers). Optional all-access subscription and an apply-agent subscription, and a one-off Agent Pass for people who bring their own AI agent: a fixed number of hours on the MCP server and a fixed number of applications, the clock starting at the agent's first call rather than at purchase; it never renews. Current prices, hours and counts are on [/pricing](/pricing); the pass is sold on the Connect-your-agent page listed under Data pages below.

Full guide text, the complete data-page map, and the CURRENT benchmark figures (median/quartile ATS scores, per-industry, with as-of date) in one fetch: [/llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt). All pages are prerendered static HTML — no JavaScript needed to read them.

## Free tools

- [Free resume scan](/): Full diagnostic report in ~20 seconds — score with audit trail, weakest bullets graded and rewritten, recruiter panel, interview questions the resume will trigger, ATS vendor checks.
- [Resume checker](/resume-checker), [ATS resume test](/ats-resume-test), [Resume score](/resume-score): The same scanner under the query each visitor asked — each page answers its own FAQs.
- [Revisar currículum (español)](/es/revisar-curriculum): Native Spanish resume checking — the engine detects Spanish terms, titles, and certifications directly.

## AI apply agent

- [The apply agent](/): Reads your CV, scores every live verified opening against it, and applies for you. What makes it different from bulk auto-appliers:
  - **It writes per role, never one blast.** Each application is drafted against that posting's own text and requirements.
  - **It answers the employer's REAL screening questions**, parsed from the actual application form on the vendors that publish them (Ashby, Breezy, Greenhouse, Pinpoint, Recruitee, Teamtailor). Where a form is not published, inferred questions are labelled as inferred and never presented as the employer's.
  - **It refuses to fabricate.** Asked about experience the CV does not show, it states the gap rather than inventing it — verified in live testing against a Kubernetes question on a CV with no Kubernetes.
  - **It never solves a CAPTCHA, spoofs a fingerprint, or evades a bot check.** On hiring systems that gate applications behind those, the agent prepares the complete application and the human submits it. This is a permanent product boundary, not a current limitation.
  - **It tracks what happens.** Every application is recorded, and because the board watches each posting's lifecycle, it can tell you when a role you applied to came down and whether it was filled or merely re-listed.

## Guides (answer-first, grounded in scanner data)

- [Why resumes get rejected before a human reads them](/guides/why-resumes-get-rejected): The four failure stages — parsing, search, skim, close read.
- [Do ATS systems auto-reject resumes?](/guides/ats-auto-rejection-myth): Mostly no — the honest mechanics, against the industry's favorite myth.
- [How to choose resume keywords](/guides/resume-keywords-guide): Job posting > O*NET > recognized titles; why stuffing backfires.
- [Career change resume playbook](/guides/career-change-resume): Bridge keywords, title translation, transition framing.
- [The resume format that survives every ATS](/guides/resume-format-that-survives-ats): Layout, sections, fonts, PDF vs DOCX — from documented parser behavior.
- [What a resume score actually means](/guides/what-resume-score-means): Scores are models with error bars; how to read one without being fooled.
- [How to put freelance work on your resume](/guides/freelance-work-on-resume): The structure decision, the bullet formula, and the metric rescue ladder for gig careers.
- [How to put fractional roles on your resume](/guides/fractional-roles-on-resume): Concurrent engagements without the job-hopper misread — the umbrella portfolio entry.

## Original data

- [What's a good ATS score? Live benchmarks](/research/ats-score-benchmarks): Median, quartiles, per-industry and experience-level benchmarks computed live from our real scan corpus — original data, honestly framed with sample sizes.
- [Explore every field on the board](/explore): Every field we serve, ordered by how many roles are open in it right now — seventeen fields plus the bucket whose field could not be read from the title, which between them reach the whole board rather than a ranked handful of employers. Open a field for the roles inside it, each priced by a live count of exactly the search its link runs; then narrow by remote, on-site, states-the-pay, a pay floor, open-to-beginners, full-time, posted-this-week, one-click apply or country, each carrying how much of the board states that thing at all — a filter can only search what employers published, so roles that did not say are hidden by it, not absent from the market. Under a field we also publish, for the slice you assembled, what our closure record does and does not say about the employers in it — how many we found, how many we hold any record for, and how many have taken roles down and not put them back up. A POSTING COMING DOWN NEVER MEANS SOMEONE WAS HIRED: a hire, a withdrawal, a cancelled requisition and a retitle are indistinguishable to us, and nothing on the page calls a closure a fill. Also carries a per-employer lookup across all 30,000+ company job boards on the board, showing what we hold beside the employer's own advertised total and the day we read it. Field counts come from the board's own facet sweep, which runs four times an hour, and the page states the time the sweep it is showing was taken; every count our collector de-duplicates is published as a floor, and no figure is shown where the query could not produce one.

## Data pages

- [Live job board](/jobs): Every posting read from the employer's own hiring system, re-verified through the day; no aggregators, no dated posting older than 30 days. Per-field pages at /jobs/field/{slug}, per-employer pages at /jobs/company/{token}.
- [Ghost Job Index](/ghost-job-index): The board's live measure of posting reality — how many roles are open, how long postings stay up, how fast they come down, and which employers are actively hiring, computed from the closure log the board keeps for every posting it has watched. A posting coming down is never called a hire: a hire, a withdrawal, a cancelled requisition and a retitle are indistinguishable from the feed.
- [Weekly Hiring Trends](/hiring-trends): Counted postings per week by each posting's own stated date, which fields are hiring, entry-level and remote shares, and closures per week from the lifecycle log. Newly catalogued employers are excluded from weekly counts, so coverage growth never reads as a hiring spike.
- [Entry-Level Index](/entry-level-index): Employers ranked by real early-career openings — internships, junior, graduate and 0–2 year roles — counted only where the posting's own title or stated requirements say so.
- [Pay Transparency Index](/pay-transparency): Which fields, hiring systems and large employers actually state pay in their postings — counted from the postings' own text and the employers' ATS fields, never estimated or modelled. Placement cannot be bought: the only way onto the page is to state pay. Recomputed hourly and stamped with the time it was measured.
- [Companies on the board](/companies): Every employer with open roles, A–Z, each with its live count and a link to its own page.
- [Hiring Data & API](/data-api): A read-only JSON API (/v1) over the live board with free self-serve keys — GET /v1/jobs, /v1/jobs/{id}, /v1/changes (what opened and closed since a timestamp, and whether each close was a genuine takedown or a re-list), /v1/companies, /v1/stats, /v1/usage, POST /v1/fit (paid). Cursor pagination, ETags. Licensing beyond the free tier: free for journalists with attribution, at cost for research, custom for commercial feeds.
- [Connect your agent — MCP server](/agents): The same board for AI agents over MCP (a plain web address; nothing to install). No key needed to start: board statistics and a capped search answer with no credential, under a small daily allowance per network address. A free key from /data-api opens every read tool; a paid key or a live Agent Pass opens résumé fit scoring; an account key with an Agent plan or Agent Pass, plus a mandate, opens the apply tools. Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and any client with a header field carry the key. claude.ai, Claude Desktop and ChatGPT have no field for a key: they sign you in instead, but only while the server's sign-in service is switched on — when it is off, a tool that needs your account answers in words and the unkeyed tools still answer; the page's "Test the server" button prints today's state. Per-app steps on the page; the tool list, the caps and the install files are in /llms-full.txt and at https://github.com/campbellaabbott-rgb/resumebooster-mcp.
- [Live ATS score benchmarks](/research/ats-score-benchmarks): Real score distributions from the scan corpus — overall median and quartiles, per-industry benchmarks, experience-level medians. Rolling 180-day window, k-anonymous aggregates only. Original data; cite with a link.
- [Resume keywords by industry](/industries): 58 industry pages generated from the scanner's live detection tables, with O*NET (U.S. Dept. of Labor) citations.
- Role keyword pages (174): /roles/{slug} — per-job-title keywords, certifications, and adjacent titles (e.g. /roles/software-engineer, /roles/registered-nurse).
- Spanish industry pages (15): /es/industrias/{slug} — native Spanish keyword data paired with English ATS terms.
- [CV standards by country](/cv-standards): Photo, length, and personal-data norms for 56 countries — the scanner's own per-market rules, with localized pages in Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, and Dutch.
- [Freelance Boost](/freelance-boost): Guided flow converting freelance projects, gig work, and side hustles into recruiter-grade resume experience. $29 one-time.
- [Resume Builder](/builder): Free structured builder with professionally typeset PDF and DOCX export.
- [Workday parsing guide](/ats/workday), [Greenhouse](/ats/greenhouse), [Lever](/ats/lever), [iCIMS](/ats/icims): How each major ATS actually parses resumes.
- [vs Jobscan](/vs/jobscan), [vs Teal](/vs/teal), [vs Rezi](/vs/rezi), [vs Kickresume](/vs/kickresume), [vs Enhancv](/vs/enhancv): Honest comparisons that name where competitors win.
- [Pricing](/pricing): One-time tools and the all-access plan.
- [Methodology](/methodology): How scoring and detection work.
- [Trust](/trust): Privacy and data handling — resumes are never stored.
- [Changelog](/changelog): Ships multiple times weekly; includes honest postmortems.
